problem: Existing ASV navigation methods and maritime DRL controllers execute goals already given in machine-readable form (coordinates, waypoints, fixed IDs). Generic language-navigation and open-vocabulary grounding models are not built for harbour distractors and do not output control-ready target states.
motivation: In ports, operators describe targets in words (e.g. 'the yellow buoy near the dock') without knowing coordinates, and a wrongly chosen buoy or vessel still yields smooth, collision-free navigation to the wrong object. Target identity ambiguity therefore has to be resolved before control, not fixed by a better policy.
key_idea: Decompose language-grounded ASV navigation into a semantic front-end (GroundingDINO candidates, harbour-aware filtering, CLIP verification) that produces a compact 8-D grounded target control state, which a PPO policy consumes for closed-loop control.
insight: Grounding is what makes target-specific navigation possible: Vision-Only and No-Target PPO reach 0-10% SR, versus 90-97% for SGNav, which matches Oracle PPO on SR. The Task 3 ablation shows filtering and verification matter most under heavy vessel clutter: SR falls from 90.0 to 40.4 without harbour-aware filtering and to 50.4 without semantic consistency, while on the simple Task 1 the drops are small. STA alone can mislead: the w/o-consistency variant on Task 1 has higher STA (99.6) but lower SR.
method: Maritime prompt construction: rule-based parsing of the description into positive prompts P+(g) (category/colour templates) and a distractor prompt set P-(g) drawn from a predefined harbour vocabulary, with target-compatible terms removed via CLIP text similarity and synonym/parent rules
Open-vocabulary candidate generation: GroundingDINO run on RGB with P+ and P- to get target boxes B+ and distractor boxes B-

Harbour-aware candidate filtering: keeps candidates passing a geometric plausibility filter (position/scale/aspect), an attribute-consistency filter (colour/category) and an IoU distractor-conflict test (d_i < tau_conf)

CLIP semantic verification: crops each remaining candidate, scores it as the max cosine similarity over the positive prompts, and picks the argmax above threshold tau_s; otherwise the target is treated as unobserved
Grounded target control state: 8-D vector [validity, x, y, w, h, area, confidence q=sigmoid(alpha*s+beta*det), cache age], with a short-term cache for lost targets; no metric distance is inferred

PPO policy execution: the policy takes [o_env, z_t] and outputs steering/yaw-rate and forward speed; reward favours progress and alignment and penalises collision and unsafe proximity; semantic refresh runs every 5 control steps (~14.8 Hz amortised)

setting.backbone: GroundingDINO + CLIP (pretrained, frozen, as inferred from the paper's description) + PPO policy (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: PPO trained in simulation only: 9,000 episodes (~3,000 per task), 3 seeds, one shared policy across tasks; no external image dataset
setting.observation: monocular onboard RGB plus environment/motion observation
setting.privileged: none for SGNav (Oracle PPO baseline uses GT target info); simulation provides stand-off/collision feedback for termination

numbers.extra: single shared policy for Tasks 1-3; simulation only

numbers_note: Custom Unity port benchmark, not a standard one. Instruction generalisation (Exp 2) results are only given in a figure (approximate text: seen SR ~90%, synonym ~87.7%, others ~85-86%). Distractor results (Exp 3) are in a table but omitted here except as described (CTR 97.7/96.0/98.0 for Tasks 1-3).
results: SGNav reaches SR 97.0/92.0/90.0% on Tasks 1-3, matching Oracle PPO (97.0/92.0/90.0) and far above Vision-Only PPO (10.3/4.1/0.0) and No-Target PPO (5.2/1.0/0.0). SR stays at 97.7-98.7% on held-out layouts, and STA is above 97% with WTR below 3% in Exp 1. It is slower and less path-efficient than Oracle.
limitations: Simulation only, with no sim-to-real validation; RGB-only perception would be fragile under fog, glare, rain and at long range

GroundingDINO is heavy (335.5 ms per semantic refresh, ~3 Hz), so refreshes every 5 steps are cached; grounding accuracy drops with complex instructions and target sets are small (3 object-level tasks); prompts are rule-based rather than free-form language understanding
Remaining failures come from control: out-of-bounds, timeouts, collisions; STA on held-out layouts is only ~67-70%
